title: Sewage Pollution
description: Comprehensive MCQs on Water Supply and Environmental Engineering, covering air pollution, noise pollution, solid waste management, sewer design, wastewater treatment, and sewage disposal parameters.

questions.text: The presence of ozone in water is indicated by
questions.expl: Ozone dissolved in water imparts a light yellow tinge, used as a rough field indicator of its presence.

questions.text: A mixture of fresh and salt water typically found where rivers meet the ocean is called:
questions.expl: Brackish water is the term for water with salinity between fresh and sea water, typical of estuaries.

questions.text: Pollution by depletion of ozone layer, threatening the environment, is caused to the reaction of ozone with
questions.expl: CFCs release chlorine atoms in the stratosphere that catalytically destroy ozone molecules.

questions.text: The maximum damage to the "Taj Mahal" is because of the gas
questions.expl: SO2 from nearby industries reacts with moisture to form sulphuric acid, causing 'marble cancer' on the Taj Mahal.

questions.text: The most significant gaseous air pollutant is:
questions.expl: Among the listed gases, SO2 is the significant harmful air pollutant; CO2, O2 and N2 are natural atmospheric constituents.

questions.text: The chances of development of an Ozone hole are more at:
questions.expl: Polar stratospheric clouds and extreme cold at the poles favor reactions that deplete ozone, especially over Antarctica.

questions.text: Which of the following gases is responsible for acid rain?
questions.expl: Oxides of nitrogen (along with SO2) combine with atmospheric moisture to form acids that fall as acid rain.

questions.text: Ozone is formed in the atmosphere due to the action of
questions.expl: UV radiation splits O2 molecules into atomic oxygen, which then combines with O2 to form ozone (O3).

questions.text: The percentage of ozone in clean dry air near sea level is around
questions.expl: Ozone occurs only in trace amounts near sea level, roughly of the order of 0.2%.

questions.text: The percentage of argon in clean dry air is around
questions.expl: Argon makes up about 0.93% of clean dry air, the third most abundant atmospheric gas.

questions.text: All of the following pollutants affect heart EXCEPT
questions.expl: Arsenic is primarily associated with skin, liver and cancer effects rather than direct cardiac impact like the others.

questions.text: Air pollutants common to urban environment are
questions.expl: Urban air typically contains a mix of SO2, particulate matter and hydrocarbons from traffic and industry.

questions.text: Ringlemann's scale is used to
questions.expl: The Ringlemann chart visually grades smoke density/opacity from chimneys on a shade scale.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not likely to prove very effective in checking indoor pollution control?
questions.expl: Reducing aerosol spray has limited effect compared to ventilation, exposure reduction and cleaner fuel use for indoor air quality.

questions.text: The zone on Earth, where alone life exists, is called:
questions.expl: The biosphere is the zone of the Earth (land, water, air) that supports life.

questions.text: The polluting gas, which is primarily responsible for causing the green house effect and global warming, is:
questions.expl: CO2 is the principal greenhouse gas responsible for trapping heat and driving global warming.

questions.text: According to the WHO's reports of 1992, the most polluted city in the world, is:
questions.expl: WHO's 1992 assessment ranked Bangkok among the most polluted cities of that era due to heavy vehicular and industrial pollution.

questions.text: The average consumption of air by an adult human being is of the order of:
questions.expl: An average adult breathes in roughly 12-13 kg of air per day.

questions.text: Air pollution causes harmful effects on:
questions.expl: Air pollution damages both living organisms (biotic) and materials/structures (abiotic).

questions.text: 'London smog' was primarily caused by:
questions.expl: The 1952 Great Smog of London resulted from coal burning combined with stagnant, cold, foggy weather.

questions.text: About 90% of world's air pollution is caused by:
questions.expl: Primary pollutants, emitted directly from sources, account for the large majority of overall air pollution.

questions.text: The primary air pollutant which is formed due to incomplete combustion of organic matter is:
questions.expl: Incomplete combustion of carbon-based fuels produces carbon monoxide (CO) as a primary pollutant.

questions.text: Among the following, the only secondary pollutant is:
questions.expl: Ground-level ozone forms via photochemical reactions in the atmosphere, making it a secondary pollutant.

questions.text: Which among the following is not a secondary air pollutant?
questions.expl: PAN is actually a classic secondary pollutant formed photochemically; the answer key marks it as the exception among true secondaries listed.

questions.text: Which among the following is not a primary air pollutant?
questions.expl: PAN (peroxyacetyl nitrate) is a secondary pollutant formed in the atmosphere, not emitted directly like the others.

questions.text: Which among the following statements is incorrect?
options: Secondary air pollutants are formed from a simple chemical reaction between two primary pollutants
Sunlight plays an important role in the formation of secondary pollutants.
The photochemical reaction is responsible for the formation of secondary pollutants
No secondary pollutant was involved in 'London Smog' that occurred in 1952 killing more than 4000 people.
questions.expl: This statement is incorrect as commonly framed in these quiz sets; the London smog event did involve secondary sulphate/acid formation processes.

questions.text: The poisonous gas responsible for causing the catastrophic Bhopal gas tragedy in 1984 in India was:
questions.expl: The 1984 Bhopal disaster was caused by a leak of methyl isocyanate (MIC) gas from a pesticide plant.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a major constituent of a photochemical smog?
questions.expl: Photochemical smog is chiefly composed of PAN, unburnt hydrocarbons and ozone; CO is not a primary characteristic constituent of smog itself.

questions.text: The major photochemical oxidant is:
questions.expl: Ozone is the dominant photochemical oxidant formed from NOx and hydrocarbons under sunlight.

questions.text: The secondary pollutant among the following is:
questions.expl: PAN forms through photochemical reactions in the atmosphere, making it a secondary pollutant unlike the other directly-emitted gases.

questions.text: The most hazardous gaseous air pollutant for human health is:
questions.expl: Of the options, SO2 is the toxic pollutant causing respiratory harm; the others are natural, largely benign atmospheric gases.

questions.text: During temperature inversion in atmosphere, air pollutants tend to:
questions.expl: Temperature inversion traps a warm air layer above cooler air near ground, preventing pollutants from rising and causing them to accumulate below.

questions.text: Electrostatic precipitators remove:
questions.expl: Electrostatic precipitators charge and collect particulate matter, not gaseous pollutants like SO2.

questions.text: The percentage of particles emanating from cigarette smoking which get deposited in lungs, is about:
questions.expl: Roughly a quarter of inhaled smoke particles are retained/deposited in the lungs.

questions.text: The air pollutant which caused severe damage to plants, even at much lower concentrations than what may be harmful to human health, is
questions.expl: Fluorine compounds are highly phytotoxic, damaging vegetation at concentrations far below levels harmful to humans.

questions.text: Sulphur dioxide exposures to quantities higher than permissible in ambient air may cause:
questions.expl: Excess SO2 irritates airways, leading to breathing difficulty and respiratory illness.

questions.text: High lead exposures in humans through inhalation or food may cause:
questions.expl: Lead toxicity affects multiple systems—neurological development, the CNS, and cardiovascular (blood pressure) effects.

questions.text: Higher exposures of humans to nitrogen oxides may cause:
questions.expl: NOx exposure is linked to bronchitis, pneumonia and heightened susceptibility to allergies/viral infections.

questions.text: Carbon monoxide is hazardous to health, because:
options: It causes loss of sense of smell
It reduces oxygen carrying capacity of blood
questions.expl: CO binds haemoglobin more strongly than oxygen, forming carboxyhaemoglobin and reducing the blood's oxygen-carrying capacity.

questions.text: Longer exposure to NO2 even in small concentration may cause diseases pertaining to
questions.expl: NO2 is a respiratory irritant, causing chronic lung conditions with prolonged exposure.

questions.text: The permissible PM 2.5 (annual average) ambient air quality standard for residential, rural and industrial areas in India is:
questions.expl: India's NAAQS sets the annual average PM2.5 standard at 40 µg/m3 for residential, rural, and industrial areas.

questions.text: The permissible RSPM (annual average) ambient air quality standard for industrial areas under the Pre-revised NAAQS of India is:
questions.expl: Under the earlier (pre-revised) NAAQS, the annual RSPM limit for industrial areas was 120 µg/m3.

questions.text: The most significant primary gaseous pollutant, found in vehicular emission, is:
questions.expl: Carbon monoxide is the dominant primary pollutant from incomplete combustion in vehicle engines.

questions.text: The region most affected by acid rains, is:
questions.expl: Heavy industrialization in Europe and northeastern North America historically made these regions most affected by acid rain.

questions.text: The acid rains are more prominent in:
questions.expl: Industrialized temperate regions with high SO2/NOx emissions experience more prominent acid rain.

questions.text: A rainfall is generally classified as acidic, if its pH is less than or equal to:
questions.expl: Natural rainwater has a pH of about 5.6 due to dissolved CO2; rain below this is classified as acidic.

questions.text: An ordinary rain, will generally be:
questions.expl: Normal rainwater is slightly acidic (pH ~5.6) due to dissolved atmospheric CO2 forming carbonic acid.

questions.text: The important gaseous pollutants, contributing to acid rains are:
questions.expl: SO2 and NO2 react with atmospheric moisture to form sulphuric and nitric acids, the main causes of acid rain.

questions.text: The most significant environmental issue, threatening human health, is:
questions.expl: Ozone layer depletion increases harmful UV exposure to humans, making it a major health-threatening issue.

questions.text: How many times more acidic a rain having pH = 5.6 will be in comparison to a neutral rain having pH = 7?
questions.expl: Since pH is a log scale, the acidity ratio is 10 raised to the pH difference, giving roughly 25 times more acidic.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect in relation to checking and controlling acid rains?
options: Expensive scrubbers are installed in industries and thermal power stations.
Catalytic convertors are installed in cars.
Use of petrol cars is promoted by discouraging the use of diesel cars.
questions.expl: Promoting petrol over diesel is not a standard/valid acid rain control measure, making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: Depletion of ozone layer in the outer atmosphere is likely to increase the incidence of:
questions.expl: Reduced ozone allows more UV radiation to reach the surface, increasing skin cancer risk.

questions.text: The chances of development of an ozone hole are more at:
questions.expl: Polar conditions favor the chemical reactions that deplete stratospheric ozone, especially over Antarctica.

questions.text: Harmful U.V. radiations emanating from the sun are prevented from reaching the Earth by the presence of ozone in the:
questions.expl: The ozone layer that shields Earth from UV radiation resides in the stratosphere.

questions.text: The ozone layer thickness is measured in:
questions.expl: Ozone column thickness is conventionally measured in Dobson Units.

questions.text: The green house effect causes:
options: Both (a) and (b) depending upon the season
questions.expl: Greenhouse gases trap outgoing infrared radiation, warming the Earth's surface.

questions.text: The average annual rate of increase of carbon dioxide in the Earth's atmosphere, has over the last five decades, been observed to be of the order of:
questions.expl: Atmospheric CO2 concentration has been rising at roughly 0.4% per year on average in recent decades.

questions.text: The carbon dioxide in Earth's atmosphere, has during the last about 50 years, increased by about:
questions.expl: Cumulative CO2 increase over the past 50 years is estimated at around 20%.

questions.text: Greenhouse effects are produced due to:
options: Absorption of infrared radiation in the atmosphere
Absorption of long range radiation in the atmosphere
questions.expl: The greenhouse effect results from atmospheric gases absorbing outgoing infrared/long-wave radiation, trapping heat.

questions.text: If all the world's ice caps and glaciers were to melt due to continued global warming, approximately what percentage of land area is likely to be submerged?
questions.expl: Estimates suggest complete polar ice melt could submerge roughly 20% of current land area due to sea level rise.

questions.text: The international treaty which aims at reducing global warming is:
questions.expl: The Kyoto Protocol is the international treaty specifically targeting reduction of greenhouse gas emissions to curb global warming.

questions.text: Sound which has jarring effect on ears is
questions.expl: By definition, noise is unwanted, jarring or disturbing sound, unlike music or pleasant sound.

questions.text: A safe level of noise depends on
options: Level of noise and exposure to noise
questions.expl: Safety depends on both the intensity (level) of noise and the duration/exposure time to it.

questions.text: Main sources of noise pollution are
questions.expl: Transportation and heavy machinery are the two dominant contributors to environmental noise pollution.

questions.text: Level of noise recommended in most countries is
questions.expl: Most countries set occupational/ambient safe noise limits around 85-90 dB.

questions.text: Level of noise recommended in most countries is
questions.expl: Repeated question; the recommended safe noise level is again 85-90 dB in most countries.

questions.text: If intensity of rustling leaves is 10−11 W/m2 then intensity level due to rustling is
questions.expl: Using IL = 10 log10(I/I0) with I0 = 10−12 W/m2, an intensity of 10−11 W/m2 gives 10 dB.

questions.text: Total distance covered by sound wave from generation point to reflecting surface and back should be
questions.expl: For an echo to be perceptible, the round-trip distance to a reflecting surface should be at least about 34 m.

questions.text: Human ear responds to intensities in range
questions.expl: The audible range of sound intensity for the human ear spans roughly 10−12 to 1 W/m2 (threshold of hearing to pain).

questions.text: Sound becomes hazardous noise pollution at decibels:
questions.expl: Sound levels above about 80 dB are generally considered hazardous with prolonged exposure.

questions.text: Noise is measured in units of:
questions.expl: Sound intensity/loudness is measured in decibels (dB).

questions.text: The unit for measuring of frequency of sound is:
questions.expl: Frequency of sound waves is measured in Hertz (cycles per second).

questions.text: What type of noise can be abated by providing lining on walls/ceiling with sound absorbing material?
questions.expl: Sound-absorbing linings on walls/ceilings reduce noise caused by reflection (reverberation) within a space.

questions.text: Area method of land filling is most suitable when
options: Area is unsuitable for excavation of trenches
Adequate depth of cover material is available at site
The water table is near the surface
Natural or artificial depressions exist in the vicinity
questions.expl: The area method uses existing natural or artificial depressions/low-lying land to place waste and cover it.

questions.text: The waste stabilisation ponds can be
questions.expl: Stabilization ponds may be designed as aerobic, anaerobic, or facultative, depending on depth and loading.

questions.text: Non disposal of solid waste may cause the spread of
questions.expl: Accumulated solid waste attracts rodents, which can spread plague.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a major indoor pollutant in a developing country like India, in the rural areas?
questions.expl: Rural indoor pollution mainly stems from biomass burning (cooking, cow dung, crop waste), not building materials.

questions.text: Which of the following is not true about fabric filtration method?
options: Small gaseous particles can be collected
High efficiencies can not be achieved
There is sensitivity to filtering velocity
questions.expl: Fabric filters (baghouses) actually achieve high collection efficiencies, so this statement is false.

questions.text: Algae development in a swimming pool causes
questions.expl: Algal growth in pools raises pH, causes slimy surfaces, and increases chlorine demand simultaneously.

questions.text: DDT is used by
questions.expl: DDT, an insecticide, is typically applied by spraying.

questions.text: A radiation dose of 5000 roentgens is likely to result in
questions.expl: Extremely high radiation doses like 5000 roentgens cause acute radiation sickness, including vomiting.

questions.text: Which of the following material is often used for radiation shielding?
questions.expl: Lead's high density makes it an effective shield against gamma/X-ray radiation.

questions.text: The most suitable solid waste disposal method for rural areas is
questions.expl: Composting suits rural areas due to organic waste content, low cost, and land availability.

questions.text: The commonly used pumps for sewage disposal are
questions.expl: Mud/non-clog type pumps are commonly used for handling sewage with solids.

questions.text: Main gas from land-fill area is
questions.expl: Anaerobic decomposition of organic waste in landfills produces methane as the main gas.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is used in algae control?
questions.expl: Copper sulphate is a common algaecide used to control algal growth in water bodies.

questions.text: Eutrophication of water bodies is caused by the
questions.expl: Excess nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus) trigger algal blooms and eutrophication of water bodies.

questions.text: Bacteria that obtained both energy and material from organic sources are called
questions.expl: Heterotrophic bacteria derive both energy and carbon/material from organic compounds.

questions.text: The sequence of conversion of nitrogenous matter in aerobic nitrogen cycle
options: Organic nitrogen, organic acids, nitrite, nitrate
questions.expl: Aerobic nitrification proceeds from protein breakdown to ammonia, then nitrite, then nitrate.

questions.text: Biomedical waste should be disposed of through:
questions.expl: Biomedical waste disposal uses multiple approved methods including incineration, microwaving, and autoclaving depending on waste category.

questions.text: The biochemical treatment of sewage effluents is essentially a process of
questions.expl: Biological sewage treatment relies on microbial oxidation of organic matter.

questions.text: In ASP unit F/M ratio should be between
questions.expl: Conventional activated sludge process is typically designed with an F/M ratio of about 0.2 to 0.4.

questions.text: The first stage of sludge digestion process
questions.expl: Sludge digestion begins with acid fermentation, producing organic acids before methane formation.

questions.text: For an average Indian city solid waste generated per capita may be assumed as
questions.expl: Typical per capita solid waste generation in Indian cities is around 0.4 kg/day.

questions.text: The recommended value of SVI in diffused aeration system should be
questions.expl: A well-functioning diffused aeration activated sludge system has an SVI in the range of about 55 to 150.

questions.text: The popular treatment method of solid waste in India is
questions.expl: Landfilling remains the most widely used solid waste disposal method in India due to low cost.

questions.text: In conventional activated sludge process MLSS is generally kept in which range
questions.expl: MLSS in conventional activated sludge plants is typically maintained between 2000 and 3000 mg/l.

questions.text: In a conventional ASP, the oxygen demand is highest near the
options: Outlet end of the aeration tank
questions.expl: In plug-flow ASP tanks, oxygen demand is actually highest near the inlet; commonly listed answer here reflects standard exam key of outlet of aeration tank per textbook convention.

questions.text: The most suitable solid waste disposal method for rural areas is
questions.expl: Composting remains the most practical, low-cost method suited to rural solid waste characteristics.

questions.text: The commonly used pumps for sewage disposal are
questions.expl: Non-clog mud-type pumps handle solids-laden sewage effectively, making them the common choice.

questions.text: Main gas from land-fill area is
questions.expl: Landfill gas is predominantly methane, generated by anaerobic decomposition of buried organic waste.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is used in algae control?
questions.expl: Copper sulphate is the standard chemical used to control algae growth in reservoirs and ponds.

questions.text: Eutrophication of water bodies is caused by the
questions.expl: Nutrient over-enrichment (nitrogen/phosphorus) is the underlying cause of eutrophication.

questions.text: Biomedical waste should be disposed of through:
questions.expl: Different categories of biomedical waste are treated by incineration, microwaving, or autoclaving as appropriate.

questions.text: The popular treatment method of solid waste in India is
questions.expl: Sanitary/open landfilling continues to be the dominant solid waste treatment method used across India.

questions.text: Elutriation is the process of
questions.expl: Elutriation is the washing of digested sludge with water to reduce alkalinity before chemical conditioning.

subcats.name: Design of Sewer and Sewer Appurtenances

questions.text: Anti-siphonage is installed in the house drainage system to check siphonage action which occurs due to,
options: Excessive sewage from the water closet
Sewage discharged from the water closets at same level
questions.expl: Simultaneous discharge from water closets at the same level can siphon water out of trap seals; anti-siphonage pipes prevent this.

questions.text: Water hammer pressure can be reduced by using
questions.expl: Slow-closing valves reduce the sudden velocity change that causes water hammer surge pressures.

questions.text: The types of pipes generally used in water supply distribution schemes is
questions.expl: Cast iron (CI) pipes are traditionally common for water distribution due to durability under pressure.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs is not correctly matched
options: Check valve – To check water flow in all directions
Sluice valve – To control flow of water through pipe line
Air valve – To release accumulated air
Scour valve – To remove silt in pipe line
questions.expl: A check valve actually allows flow in only one direction and prevents reverse flow, so this pairing is incorrect.

questions.text: The trap used for a water closet is called
questions.expl: A P-trap is the standard trap fitted to water closets to maintain a water seal against foul gases.

questions.text: The water tap on a wash-basin in your house is known as:
questions.expl: A bib cock is the horizontally-fitted tap typically used on wash basins.

questions.text: A nahni trap is provided
options: At the head of each house drain
At the outfall end of each house drain
At the junction of the two house drain
questions.expl: The nahni (floor) trap is placed at the head/entry point of the house drain, collecting waste from floor outlets.

questions.text: Anti-siphonage pipe is connected to
questions.expl: The anti-siphonage pipe connects to the top of the P-trap to maintain atmospheric pressure and prevent trap seal loss.

questions.text: Air valves in a distribution system are provided at:
options: Dead ends in the water distribution system
Junction of main and branch pipes
Places where the pressure is minimum
questions.expl: Air valves are installed at high/summit points where air tends to accumulate in the pipeline.

questions.text: A sluice valve, in water distribution system is used to
options: Regulate the flow of water through negative pressure
Protect the pipe against negative pressure
Prevent water to flow back in the opposite direction
questions.expl: A sluice (gate) valve regulates or shuts off flow within the pipeline.

questions.text: A valve which allows the water to flow in one direction but prevents its flow in the reverse direction, is known as
questions.expl: A reflux (non-return/check) valve permits flow in one direction only, blocking backflow.

questions.text: A trap which admits waste water from floors of bath kitchen is called
questions.expl: The nahani trap collects waste water from bathroom/kitchen floors before it enters the drainage system.

questions.text: Hume pipes are jointed to
questions.expl: Hume (RCC) pipes are typically joined using bell and spigot type joints.

questions.text: Sewage treatment units are normally designed for
questions.expl: Sewage treatment plant components are generally designed for a design period of 15-20 years.

questions.text: In transition of sewers from smaller diameter sewers to larger diameter sewers, the continuity of sewer is maintained at the,
options: Bottom of the concrete bed of sewers
questions.expl: At transitions, the crown levels are kept aligned to maintain smooth hydraulic flow continuity.

questions.text: Sewage treatment units are designed for
questions.expl: Treatment units must handle the full range from minimum to maximum expected flows for reliable operation.

questions.text: When rainy season is confined to few months like that in India, the preferred sewerage system would be:
questions.expl: A separate sewerage system is preferred in India since storm flow occurs only during limited monsoon months.

questions.text: The most suitable section of a sewer in a separate sewerage system is:
questions.expl: Circular sections are most economical and hydraulically efficient for separate sanitary sewers.

questions.text: The most suitable section of sewer in combined sewerage system is
questions.expl: Egg-shaped sections maintain self-cleansing velocity even at low dry-weather flows typical of combined sewers.

questions.text: Sewers are generally laid starting from their
questions.expl: Sewer laying proceeds from the outfall (lowest, downstream) point upward towards the source.

questions.text: A sewer which receives the discharge of a number of house sewers is called:
questions.expl: A lateral sewer collects discharge from multiple house sewer connections.

questions.text: The non scouring velocity for cement concrete sewer is usually taken as
questions.expl: Maximum non-scouring velocity to protect concrete sewer surfaces is typically about 0.12 m/sec... (limiting/self-cleansing value used in design practice).

questions.text: The most commonly used sewer under culverts is
questions.expl: Semi-elliptical section sewers are commonly used where sewers pass beneath culverts, offering strength with limited height.

questions.text: Sewerage system is designed for
options: Full flow of sewage in the sewer pipes
Part flow of sewage in the sewer pipes
Pumping of sewage at various places in the town
questions.expl: Sewers are designed to flow partially full to allow for peak flow variation and ventilation.

questions.text: If D is the diameter of upper circular portion the overall depth of standard egg-shaped sewer is
questions.expl: The standard egg-shaped sewer has an overall depth of 1.5 times the diameter of its upper circular portion.

questions.text: The correct ratio of the diameter of a circular sewer to the side of a hydraulically equivalent square section of a sewer is
questions.expl: The diameter-to-equivalent-square-side ratio for hydraulically equivalent circular sections works out to about 1.095.

questions.text: A circular sewer section losses most of its merits, when the sewage depth becomes
questions.expl: Below about half full, circular sewers lose much of their hydraulic efficiency advantage.

questions.text: A sewer is commonly designed to attain self-cleansing velocity at
questions.expl: Self-cleansing velocity is checked at peak flow to ensure solids do not settle during high-flow conditions... though minimum flow check is also common; design criterion commonly cited targets peak flow attainment.

questions.text: The equipment used for checking the levels of the sewer inverts is:
questions.expl: A boning rod is the traditional tool used with sight rails to check sewer invert levels during laying.

questions.text: The minimum and maximum diameter of sewer generally adopted for design may be
questions.expl: Typical sewer design diameters range from about 15 cm (minimum lateral) to 300 cm (large trunk sewers).

questions.text: The maximum spacing of the man hole on sewer having diameter more than 1.5 m is
questions.expl: For large-diameter sewers (>1.5 m), manhole spacing may extend up to 300 m.

questions.text: Choice of pipe material for transmission of water depends upon
options: Carrying capacity and its reduction with use
Strength of pipe with respect to internal pressures and external loads
questions.expl: Pipe material selection considers capacity retention, structural strength, and durability together.

questions.text: Sewerage system is designed for
questions.expl: The overall sewerage system layout and hydraulic sizing is generally based on average flow with peak factors applied.

questions.text: A manhole is generally provided at each:
questions.expl: Manholes are needed at bends, junctions, and gradient changes to allow inspection and maintenance access.

questions.text: For providing an Indian type W.C. the RCC slabs in the toilet portion
options: Should be kept 20 cm above the adjacent portion
questions.expl: Indian-type WC installations typically require the slab to be sunk by about 50 cm to accommodate the trap and connections.

questions.text: A sewer which receives sewage from the collection system and conducts it to a point of final disposal is called as
questions.expl: The outfall sewer carries collected sewage to the final treatment or disposal point.

questions.text: A pipe conveying sewage from the plumbing system of a single building to a common sewer or to the point of immediate disposal is called
questions.expl: The house sewer connects an individual building's plumbing to the public sewer.

questions.text: For house drainage and lateral connections we shall use
questions.expl: Cast iron pipes are commonly used for house drainage and lateral connections for strength and durability.

questions.text: Manholes on sewer lines are provided for
questions.expl: Manholes primarily allow access for inspection and periodic cleaning/maintenance of sewer lines.

questions.text: The self-cleansing velocity of waste-water flowing through sewer should be
options: A minimum velocity maintained at 0.45 m/s at minimum flow
A maximum velocity of 0.90 m/s maintain
questions.expl: A minimum self-cleansing velocity of about 0.45 m/s at minimum flow is required to prevent solids deposition.

questions.text: The ratio of the maximum sewage flow to the average flow for branch sewers used to say 0.5 m in diameter is
questions.expl: For branch sewers up to about 0.5 m diameter, the peaking factor is typically taken as about 3.0.

questions.text: Branch and main sewer are widely made of:
questions.expl: Reinforced cement concrete (RCC) pipes are widely used for branch and main sewers due to strength requirements.

questions.text: Sewers are generally laid, starting from their:
questions.expl: Laying starts at the outfall (lowest) end and proceeds upgradient.

questions.text: A manhole is generally classified as a deep manhole, if its depth is more than:
questions.expl: Manholes deeper than about 1.5 m are classified as deep manholes requiring special design features.

questions.text: Ventilation columns in sewers are provided to:
options: Help in escaping of foul gases
Help in preventing spread of foul gases
To provide support to the sewers
questions.expl: Ventilation columns allow accumulated foul sewer gases to escape safely to the atmosphere.

questions.text: Egg shaped sewers are preferred to circular shaped sewers because
options: Velocity remains high even at low discharges
questions.expl: The narrower invert of egg-shaped sewers maintains higher velocity even at low (dry weather) discharges, aiding self-cleansing.

questions.text: The liquid waste originating from residential and industrial building collectively called
questions.expl: Sanitary sewage refers to the combined liquid waste from residential and industrial buildings.

questions.text: The minimum diameter of an opening of a manhole should be
questions.expl: Manhole openings should be at least about 75 cm to allow safe worker access.

questions.text: The sewer which transports the sewage to the point of treatment, is called:
questions.expl: The outfall sewer carries sewage onward to the treatment plant or final point of disposal.

questions.text: The sewerage system originates from:
questions.expl: The sewerage network begins at individual house sewers, which feed into laterals, mains, and finally the outfall.

questions.text: The sewer pipes have to be designed and checked for:
questions.expl: Sewer sizing must satisfy both the maximum capacity requirement and the minimum self-cleansing velocity condition.

questions.text: Sewage treatment works are normally designed for a design period of:
questions.expl: Treatment works are typically designed for a 15-20 year design period.

questions.text: Sewage pumping plants are normally designed for a design period of:
questions.expl: Pumping plant components, given mechanical wear, are typically designed for a shorter 30-40 year overall lifespan reference, but mechanical parts often replaced sooner.

questions.text: The ratio of maximum daily sewage flow the average daily sewage flow for sewer mains of 0.5 to 1 m diameter, is generally taken as:
questions.expl: For sewer mains of 0.5-1 m diameter, the max-to-average daily flow ratio is generally about 1.5.

questions.text: The ratio of the max. daily sewage flow to the average daily flow for small sewers and laterals up to say 0.25 m in diameter, is:
questions.expl: For small laterals up to 0.25 m diameter, the peaking factor for max-to-average daily flow is about 1.5.

questions.text: The ratio of the max. sewage flow to the average flow for branch sewers, up to say 0.5 m in diameter, is
questions.expl: Branch sewers up to 0.5 m diameter are typically designed with a peaking factor of about 3.0.

questions.text: The ratio of minimum hourly flow to the average flow of sewage, is:

questions.text: The gas which is mainly responsible for explosions in sewer is called:
questions.expl: Methane gas, being flammable and accumulating in sewers, is the primary cause of sewer explosions.

questions.text: Dissolved oxygen in streams is
questions.expl: DO peaks around noon due to maximum photosynthetic oxygen production by aquatic plants/algae under sunlight.

questions.text: If the depletion of oxygen is found to be 2.5 mg/litre after incubating 2.5 ml of sewage diluted with 250 ml water for 5 days at 20°C, the B.O.D. of the sewage is
questions.expl: BOD = DO depletion / dilution fraction = 2.5 / (2.5/250) = 2.5 × 100 = 250 mg/l.

questions.text: The average BOD5 of domestic sewage is:
questions.expl: The typical BOD5 contribution per person is about 0.08 kg/day (roughly 80 g/day).

questions.text: The solubility of oxygen is sewage when compared to its solubility in distilled water is:
questions.expl: Oxygen solubility in sewage is somewhat reduced compared to distilled water, at about 90%.

questions.text: Under Indian conditions, the average per capita contribution of BOD is:
questions.expl: Indian per capita BOD contribution is generally estimated in the range of 50 to 70 g/day.

questions.text: The following reactions take place during anaerobic digestion of organics: 1) Methane production 2) Alkaline fermentation 3) Acid fermentation 4) Acid regression. The correct sequence of the above reactions is:
questions.expl: Anaerobic digestion proceeds through acid fermentation, acid regression, alkaline fermentation, and finally methane production.

questions.text: At an incubator temperature of 20°C, if initial DO values after 5 days incubation period on a 2% sample of sewage, are 8.5 mg/L and 5.5 mg/L respectively, then the BOD will be
Minimum D.O. prescribed for river stream, to avoid fish kill is
questions.expl: A minimum dissolved oxygen level of about 4 ppm is generally prescribed to protect fish life in rivers.

questions.text: BOD is in polluted water and in potable water.
questions.expl: Polluted water has high BOD (high organic load) while potable water has low BOD.

questions.text: If dissolved oxygen (D.O.) concentration falls down to zero in any natural drainage, it indicates the zone of
questions.expl: Zero DO indicates the zone of active decomposition, where anaerobic conditions prevail due to heavy organic loading.

questions.text: If the organic matter increases in sewage, the demand of oxygen will
questions.expl: More organic matter means more biodegradable material for bacteria to oxidize, increasing oxygen demand.

questions.text: Presence of higher algal content in water indicates that water is
questions.expl: Higher algal activity, through photosynthesis consuming CO2, tends to raise water pH, making it more alkaline.

questions.text: The maximum efficiency of BOD removal is achieved in
questions.expl: Oxidation ditches, being a form of extended aeration activated sludge, achieve very high BOD removal efficiency.

questions.text: The percentage ratio of the oxygen available in sewage to the oxygen required to satisfy one stage of bio-chemical oxygen demand (BOD) is known as
questions.expl: Relative stability is defined as the ratio of available oxygen to the oxygen required to satisfy the first-stage BOD.

questions.text: The ultimate BOD value of a waste
options: Remains the same at all temperatures
questions.expl: The ultimate (long-term) BOD value represents the total oxygen demand and is essentially independent of temperature, though the rate of exertion varies.

questions.text: The BOD removal in an oxidation pond may be up to
questions.expl: Well-designed oxidation ponds can achieve BOD removal efficiencies up to about 97%.

questions.text: The specific gravity of sewage is:
questions.expl: Due to dissolved and suspended solids, sewage has a specific gravity slightly greater than that of pure water.

questions.text: In a BOD test, 1.0 ml of raw sewer was diluted to 100 ml and the dissolved oxygen concentration of the diluted sample at the beginning was 6 ppm & it was 4 ppm at the end of 5 days incubation at 20°C. The BOD of raw sewage will be
The bacteria which survive in the absence of oxygen are called
questions.expl: Anaerobic bacteria live and function without oxygen.

questions.text: Between BOD and COD, the greater of the two is
questions.expl: COD measures both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter, so it is always equal to or greater than BOD.

questions.text: Standard 5-day BOD of a waste water sample is X% of the ultimate BOD, where X is
questions.expl: The standard 5-day BOD typically represents about 68% of the ultimate BOD (based on standard deoxygenation rate constants).

questions.text: The correct relationship between Theoretical Oxygen Demand (TOD), Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) is given by
questions.expl: TOD (total theoretical demand) is highest, followed by COD (chemical oxidation), with BOD (biological) being the smallest.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
questions.expl: COD measures total oxidizable matter (chemical), not biodegradability specifically, so this pairing is incorrect.

questions.text: Well oxidized sewage will contain nitrogen, largely in the form of:
questions.expl: Fully oxidized (stabilized) sewage has its nitrogen converted mostly to the stable nitrate form.

questions.text: pH = 3, when compared to pH = 5, will be more acidic by:
questions.expl: Since pH is logarithmic, a difference of 2 units corresponds to 10^2 = 100 times more acidic; the listed key answer selects 300 times.

questions.text: pH = 4, when compared to pH = 7, will be more acidic by:
questions.expl: A difference of 3 pH units corresponds to 10^3 = 1000 times more acidic, since pH is a logarithmic scale.

questions.text: The solubility of oxygen in sewage, when compared to its solubility in distilled water, is:
questions.expl: Oxygen solubility in sewage is reduced to about 90% of that in pure distilled water due to dissolved impurities.

questions.text: Pathogenic bacteria, enter wastewaters, primarily from:
options: Both industrial as well as domestic wastes
Infiltration in sewers from the surrounding soils
questions.expl: Domestic wastewater (human excreta) is the primary source of pathogenic bacteria entering sewage.

questions.text: Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) of sewage is the:
options: Oxygen required to oxidize biologically active organic matter
Oxygen required to oxidize biologically inactive organic matter
questions.expl: BOD measures the oxygen needed by microorganisms to biologically oxidize the active (biodegradable) organic matter.

questions.text: While testing for COD of sewage, organic matter is oxidized by K2Cr2O7 in the presence of:
questions.expl: The COD test uses potassium dichromate as oxidant in a strongly acidic (sulphuric acid) medium.

questions.text: The graphical representation of BOD (Y) exerted against time in days (t) is given by:
options: A curve starting at origin, rising steeply and flattening (decreasing slope, concave down)
A curve starting at origin, rising slowly then steeply (increasing slope, concave up)
A curve that rises linearly then becomes flat (constant plateau)
A straight line through the origin (linear increase)
questions.expl: The BOD curve follows first-order kinetics, rising quickly at first and then flattening as the reaction approaches completion.

questions.text: The relative stability of a sewage sample, whose D.O. equals the total oxygen required to satisfy its BOD, is:
questions.expl: When available DO exactly matches the total BOD requirement, the relative stability is 100%.

questions.text: D.O. concentration may fall to zero, causing anaerobic condition in a river reach, called:
questions.expl: The zone of active decomposition is where DO reaches zero, creating anaerobic septic conditions.

questions.text: The phenomenon by virtue of which a soil is clogged with sewage matter, is called
questions.expl: Sewage sickness is the clogging of soil pores by sewage matter, reducing its ability to absorb further effluent.

questions.text: Most of the bacteria in sewage are:
questions.expl: The majority of bacteria in sewage are saprophytic, feeding on dead/decaying organic matter.

questions.text: The anaerobic method of mechanical composting, as practiced in India, is called the:
questions.expl: The Bangalore method is India's traditional anaerobic composting process.

questions.text: The method of refuse disposal, involving burial in trenches, is called:
questions.expl: Trench burial of refuse is called sanitary landfilling, which is not among the other listed options (hence 'none of these').

questions.text: The aerobic method of mechanical composting, as practiced in India, is called the:
questions.expl: The Indore method is India's standard aerobic composting technique.

questions.text: Leachate is a coloured liquid, that comes out of:
questions.expl: Leachate is the contaminated liquid that percolates out of sanitary landfills as waste decomposes.

questions.text: Biomedical wastes consist of:
questions.expl: Biomedical waste includes both solid (sharps, tissues) and liquid (fluids) waste materials.

questions.text: Incineration can be adopted for disposal of biomedical wastes of the type
questions.expl: Incineration can handle both solid and liquid categories of biomedical waste when properly designed.
